title: Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change sugar research levy arrangements and transfer the Sugar Research and Development Corporation's activities, assets and liabilities to an industry services body.
It would set the levy at 70 cents per tonne, shared equally by producers and processors, and broaden the circumstances attracting the levy.
The bill would support the companion sugar research services legislation, with levy instalment arrangements starting on 1 March 2014 and transitional provisions for winding up the corporation.
changes: The levy rate could be varied by regulation without a statutory maximum.
Cane leaves purchased or processed separately would fall outside the levy.
Monthly levy liabilities would be split into a 60 per cent first instalment and a 40 per cent later instalment.
Transfers to the new body would be exempt from state and territory stamp duty and other taxes.
summary.affected: Sugar cane producers and processors, the Sugar Research and Development Corporation and the new industry services body are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the companion Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, which transfers 75 per cent of the Sugar Research and Development Corporation's assets to the new industry body on its declaration and winds up the corporation by 30 September 2013, with the levy increase taking effect from 1 July 2013.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills as a reform backed by most of the industry, under which Sugar Research Australia would replace separate research bodies and receive a 70c per tonne levy paid equally by growers and mills, while raising concerns about consultation, regional research, conflicts of interest and the legislation's rushed 1 July 2013 commencement.

speeches.speaker: George Christensen
speeches.brief: Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills, saying they would consolidate research functions in Sugar Research Australia, reduce duplication and secure funding through a 70c per tonne levy, while urging swift passage to provide certainty for research staff and the industry's future.

acts.title: Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Act 2013
